items.title: The prognostic significance of Lipoprotein(a) is modified by obstructive sleep apnea in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
items.abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established residual cardiovascular risk factor in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), a common cardiometabolic disorder, may modify the association between Lp(a) and cardiovascular outcomes. Therefore, the present study aimed to further evaluate whether OSA statistically modifies the association between Lp(a) and long-term cardiovascular outcomes in a prospective cohort of patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). A total of 1027 consecutive patients who underwent PCI and sleep study were initially screened. After prespecified exclusions, 846 patients were included in the final analysis. Moderate-to-severe OSA was defined as an AHI ≥15 events/h, whereas patients with an AHI <15 events/h constituted the comparison group. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), including cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, heart failure and stroke. During 3.5(2.8-4.2) years of follow-up, 169(19.97%) cardiovascular events occurred. Post-PCI patients who experienced MACEs exhibited significantly higher Lp(a) levels compared to those without MACEs (median 26.50 vs.11.00 mg/dL, P 30mg/dL) were associated with increased risks of cardiovascular events with hazard ratios of 1.881 (95%CI 1.168-3.029, P 30 mg/dL) was associated with a 2.286-fold higher risk of MACEs compared to Lp(a) (<10 mg/dL), whereas no statistically significant association was observed among patients with AHI <15 events/h. OSA status may statistically modify the association between elevated Lp(a) and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. These findings support further investigation into the prognostic relevance of combined OSA and Lp(a) assessment, while additional studies are needed to validate these observations and determine their implications for clinical practice.

items.title: Development and explainability of a machine-learning model for predicting in-hospital mortality after percutaneous coronary intervention for unprotected left main coronary artery disease.
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of mortality after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for unprotected left main coronary artery (LMCA) disease is essential for risk stratification. We compared machine-learning (ML) models with the EuroSCORE II and the SYNTAX score for predicting in-hospital mortality and used explainable artificial intelligence to identify the most important predictors. In this subanalysis of the Gulf-LM registry, 1,205 patients who underwent PCI for unprotected LMCA disease between 2015 and 2019 were analyzed; 45 (3.7%) died in hospital. Twenty-four baseline pre-procedural variables were used, with the EuroSCORE II and SYNTAX score retained continuously. Fourteen ML algorithms and the traditional scores were evaluated by cross-validation; performance was summarized from pooled out-of-fold predictions with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Discrimination was assessed by the AUROC and AUPRC, and calibration by the Brier score, calibration slope, and calibration-in-the-large; the model was interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). The random forest achieved the best performance, with an AUROC of 0.904 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.859-0.941), an AUPRC of 0.335, and a Brier score of 0.030, outperforming the EuroSCORE II (AUROC 0.82) and the SYNTAX score (AUROC 0.56). In patient-level paired comparisons, the random forest improved discrimination over the EuroSCORE II (ΔAUROC +0.083) but not significantly over a parsimonious four-predictor model, and a nested cross-validation gave a selection-corrected AUROC of 0.885 (0.841-0.924), the internally estimated discrimination of the AUROC-based selection procedure. Calibration estimates were compatible with ideal calibration but imprecise (calibration-in-the-large 0.02; slope 1.20, 95% CI 0.93-1.57; mean predicted mortality 3.7% versus observed 3.7%), and the model stratified patients into groups with observed in-hospital mortality of 0.3%, 4.0%, and 15.1%. SHAP analysis, corroborated by permutation importance, identified the EuroSCORE II, STEMI presentation, cardiogenic shock, and tachyarrhythmia as the strongest predictors of mortality. An explainable random-forest model discriminated better than the EuroSCORE II and the SYNTAX score for predicting in-hospital mortality after PCI for unprotected LMCA disease, with descriptive risk stratification including a low observed mortality rate in the lowest-risk group. This is a model development study with internal validation only, and external validation is needed.

items.title: A small angle of shunting and detectable shunting inlet may predict successful exclusive transvenous closure of patent ductus arteriosus with a 3-year follow-up.
items.abstract: The transvenous V-method simplifies transcatheter patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) closure compared with the arteriovenous (AV) method and retrograde transarterial coil occlusion, with fewer complications, but it carries variable failure rates. This study aimed to identify preoperative transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) predictors for V-method failure and establish a practical model to optimize procedural strategies. A total of 403 consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter PDA closure in Fujian Medical University Union Hospital between October 2014 and July 2019 were retrospectively enrolled and randomly split to training ( n  = 282) and internal validation ( n  = 121) cohorts at a 7:3 ratio. LASSO regression was performed to screen independent predictors. Model performance was validated via ROC, calibration and decision curve analysis. All patients received standardized 3-year postoperative follow-up. Overall, 323 patients completed V-method closure, and 80 converted to the AV-method. The median age was 7 years (6 months-73 years) and an average PDA size of 4.43 mm (1.0mm-14.5 mm). Large shunt angle (defined as shunt beam-PDA inlet plane angle; A larger angle may indicate more perpendicular insertion to the pulmonary artery wall) and undetectable PDA shunting inlet on preoperative TTE were independent predictors of V-method failure. The dual-index model achieved excellent predictive performance with AUCs of 0.933 (training) and 0.910 (validation), along with favorable calibration and clinical net benefit. The optimal cut-off value for the model was defined as an undetectable PDA shunting inlet or a shunt angle > 81.61°, with a sensitivity of 89.5% and a specificity of 96.4%. At 3-year follow-up, no signal of excess harm was detected in either group. A small angle of shunting and detectable shunting inlet by echocardiography may predict successful exclusive transvenous PDA closure. The 3-year follow-up suggested the safety and efficacy of the exclusive transvenous access.

items.title: Spanish cardiac catheterization in congenital heart diseases registry. Fifth official report from the ACI-SEC and GTH-SECPCC (2024).
items.abstract: The Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (ACI-SEC) and the Interventional Working Group of the Spanish Society of Pediatric Cardiology (GTH-SECPCC) introduce their annual report on interventional activity in congenital heart diseases in 2024. Spanish centers with cath labs performing interventional procedures for congenital heart disease were invited to participate. Data were collected through an online platform and analyzed by an external company in collaboration with members of the ACI-SEC and GTH-SECPCC. A total of 22 cath lab units from 17 public and 3 private hospitals participated in the registry. Furthermore, the analysis included data on interventional procedures for adult congenital heart disease performed at an additional 98 adult cardiology units reporting activity in congenital heart disease. These units were among the 118 hospitals participating in the 2024 Spanish cardiac catheterization in congenital heart diseases registry of the ACI-SEC. A total of 1888 diagnostic studies were recorded, representing a 67.5% increase compared with 2023, as well as 3711 interventional catheterizations, representing a 3.8% decrease. Of these procedures, 2287 (61.6%) were performed in patients older than 18 years, representing a 6.2% decrease compared with 2023. The most frequent procedures were patent foramen ovale closure (1392 cases) and atrial septal defect closure (641 cases), followed by patent ductus arteriosus closure (368 cases), pulmonary artery branch angioplasty (236 cases), angioplasty for aortic coarctation (172 cases), transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation (160 cases), and ventricular septal defect closure (84 cases). Among procedures for which outcomes were reported, the success rate was 96.9%, the major complication rate was 1.9%, and the in-hospital mortality rate was 0.3%. All interventional procedures showed excellent safety and efficacy outcomes despite a slight reduction in the overall procedural volume compared with 2023. La Asociación de Cardiología Intervencionista de la Sociedad Española de Cardiología (ACI-SEC) y el Grupo de Trabajo de Hemodinámica de la Sociedad Española de Cardiología Pediátrica y Cardiopatías Congénitas (GTH-SECPCC) presentan su informe anual de actividad hemodinámica en cardiopatías congénitas correspondiente al año 2024. Se invitó a participar a los centros españoles con laboratorio de hemodinámica y actividad intervencionista en cardiopatías congénitas. Los datos se recogieron mediante una plataforma telemática y su análisis lo realizó una empresa externa en colaboración con miembros de la ACI-SEC y el GTH-SECPCC. Participaron en el registro 22 unidades de hemodinámica que corresponden a 17 hospitales públicos y 3 privados. Se incorporaron al análisis los datos de intervencionismo en cardiopatías congénitas del adulto aportados por otras 98 unidades de adultos que registraron algún tipo de actividad en enfermedades congénitas, de los 118 hospitales participantes en el registro de hemodinámica y cardiología intervencionista de la ACI-SEC del año 2024. Se registraron 1.888 estudios diagnósticos (un 67,5% más que en 2023) y 3.711 cateterismos intervencionistas (un 3,8% menos que en 2023), de los que 2.287 (61,6%) se realizaron en mayores de 18 años (un 6,2% menos que en 2023). Los procedimientos más frecuentes fueron los cierres de foramen oval permeable (1.392 casos) y de comunicación interauricular (641), seguidos del cierre de ductus persistente (368), la angioplastia de ramas pulmonares (236), la angioplastia de la coartación de aorta (172), el implante de válvula pulmonar percutánea (160) y el cierre de comunicación interventricular (84). El porcentaje de éxito en los procedimientos intervencionistas en que se notificó fue del 96,9%, con una tasa de complicaciones mayores del 1,9% y una mortalidad intrahospitalaria del 0,3%. Todas las técnicas intervencionistas han mostrado excelentes resultados de seguridad y eficacia, y ha habido una ligera reducción del volumen global de procedimientos intervencionistas respecto a 2023.

items.title: SELUTION SLR sirolimus-eluting balloon compared with the Pantera Lux paclitaxel drug-coated balloon in the management of de novo coronary lesions.
items.abstract: Drug-coated balloons are an emerging stentless therapeutic option for the treatment of de novo coronary artery disease. Although paclitaxel-coated balloons remain the current standard, concerns regarding delayed vascular healing and potential local toxicity have driven the development of sirolimus-eluting balloons (SEB). This study aimed to compare the safety and efficacy profile of the novel SELUTION SLR SEB with the established Pantera Lux paclitaxel-coated balloon in a real-world cohort of patients with de novo coronary artery disease. We conducted a prospective, single-center registry included 257 patients with 316 de novo coronary lesions treated with drug-coated balloon-only percutaneous coronary intervention from 2023 through 2024. Patients were treated with either the SELUTION SLR sirolimus-eluting balloon or the Pantera Lux paclitaxel-coated balloon. A 1-year follow-up was conducted to assess major adverse cardiovascular events, target lesion failure (TLF), and target lesion revascularization (TLR), which were descriptively compared across groups. Baseline clinical and angiographic characteristics were well balanced. At the 1-year follow-up, the overall rate of major adverse cardiovascular events was 5.8%, with no significant differences across treatment groups. The rates of TLF and TLR were low and comparable. However, patients treated with the SELUTION SLR experienced fewer procedural complications, including a lower rate of mild coronary dissections (6.7% vs 14.7%; P = .043) and no-reflow events (0.0% vs 2.7%; P = .036). The SELUTION SLR SEB demonstrated efficacy vs the Pantera Lux, with fewer procedural complications. These findings support the selective use of SELUTION SLR as a stentless treatment strategy and highlight the need for larger randomized trials to confirm long-term comparative outcomes. Los balones farmacoactivos representan una alternativa emergente sin stent para el tratamiento de la enfermedad coronaria de novo . Aunque los balones recubiertos de paclitaxel constituyen el estándar actual, las preocupaciones sobre el retraso en la cicatrización y la toxicidad vascular han favorecido el desarrollo de balones liberadores de sirolimus. El objetivo fue comparar la seguridad y la eficacia del balón liberador de sirolimus SELUTION SLR frente al balón recubierto de paclitaxel Pantera Lux en pacientes con enfermedad coronaria de novo en la práctica clínica real. Registro prospectivo y unicéntrico que incluye 257 pacientes con 316 lesiones de novo tratados mediante intervención coronaria percutánea exclusivamente con balón farmacoactivo entre 2023 y 2024. Los pacientes recibieron SELUTION SLR (sirolimus) o Pantera Lux (paclitaxel). El seguimiento a 1 año evaluó los eventos cardiacos adversos mayores, el fracaso de la lesión diana y la revascularización de la lesión diana, analizados de forma descriptiva. Las características clínicas y angiográficas basales fueron comparables entre los grupos. Al año, la tasa global de eventos cardiacos adversos mayores fue del 5,8%, sin diferencias significativas. El fracaso de la lesión diana y la revascularización de la lesión diana fueron bajos y similares. Sin embargo, el grupo con SELUTION SLR presentó menos complicaciones intraprocedimiento, incluidas disecciones coronarias leves (6,7% frente a 14,7 %, p = 0,043) y fenómenos de no reflujo (0,0 % frente a 2,7 %, p = 0,036). El balón liberador de sirolimus SELUTION SLR mostró una eficacia comparable al Pantera Lux, con menos complicaciones intraprocedimiento, lo que apoya su uso selectivo como estrategia sin stent y señala la necesidad de ensayos aleatorizados de mayor tamaño.

items.title: Dynamic changes in cytokine levels as potential prognostic biomarkers in cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have reshaped cancer therapy, yet fewer than 20% of patients achieve durable benefit and many develop immune-related adverse events, highlighting the need for accessible biomarkers to support treatment decisions. Circulating cytokines obtained through liquid biopsy offer a minimally invasive means to monitor systemic immune activity and represent exploratory, hypothesis-generating indicators of immune modulation during ICI therapy. We retrospectively analyzed clinical data and paired plasma samples from patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors treated within early-phase ICI-based trials at IRCCS Humanitas Research Hospital (2019-2023). Blood was collected at baseline and at first radiologic assessment. Thirteen cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-8, CXCL10, CCL2, TGF-β1) were quantified using a multiplex bead-based assay, and longitudinal changes were classified as positive, negative, or null. Exploratory associations with disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS), and treatment duration were evaluated. Immunohistochemistry for CD3, CD68, and CD66b was performed to explore descriptive correlations between cytokine modulation and tumor immune contexture. Sixty-six patients were included. Positive IL-1β variation was associated with higher DCR (p=0.022). OS showed exploratory associations with positive changes in IL-1β, IL-12p70, and IL-4. Concordant cytokine modulation across these cytokines was frequent (all p<0.001). Increased IFN-γ correlated with longer treatment duration. Patients with at least one positive cytokine change displayed higher CD3+ T-cell density and lower CD66b+ neutrophil infiltration. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that paired longitudinal cytokine profiling may complement tissue-based biomarkers and inform future personalized immunotherapy strategies.

items.title: Deep immune profiling of stage III resected melanoma patients undergoing anti-PD1 adjuvant therapy unveils critical immunophenotypes associated with tumor recurrence or adverse effects.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockers (ICB) are standard of care as adjuvant therapy for patients with resected high-risk melanoma, yet many patients suffer from immune-related adverse effects (AEs), while others experienced tumor relapse. Identification of biomarkers capable of predicting tumor relapse or understanding the occurrence of AEs remains a major challenge to improve outcomes and develop efficient and more tolerated strategies. We explored the immune landscape at baseline and during treatment in blood of resected stage III melanoma patients treated with anti-PD-1 adjuvant therapy and evaluated its association with tumor recurrence and occurrence of AEs. Through a comprehensive immunomonitoring based on multi-parametric flow cytometry combined with multiplex immunoassays, we depicted DC, monocyte, and effector subsets and examined their detailed phenotypic and functional features together with soluble factors in plasma. Immune features were compared between groups using both supervised and unsupervised computational machine-learning analyses. We revealed distinct immune landscape between non-relapsing (NP) and progressive (PD) melanoma patients as well as immune profiles associated with occurrence of AEs, with modulated innate and adaptive immunophenotypes together with functional perturbations. We highlighted innovative predictive signatures associated with clinical outcome: plasmatic ULBP3/4 and CD73 levels, importance of DC3 and monocyte subsets, relevance of new checkpoints (Gal9/TIM3 and CD155/TIGIT). We uncovered candidate immunophenotypes associated with tumor recurrence or AEs in stage III melanoma patients treated by anti-PD1 adjuvant therapy. Deciphering such challenges is promising to optimize ICB efficacy while reducing AEs, and design pertinent combination strategies to achieve better clinical successes in future.

items.title: The Potential Role and Mechanism of Cuproptosis in Osteosarcoma Treatment.
items.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is a highly aggressive primary bone malignancy that predominantly affects adolescents and is characterized by invasiveness and metastasis. However, the prognosis of OS is still unsatisfactory and constrained by the limited efficacy of conventional therapies, highlighting the urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. Recently, cuproptosis, a novel programmed cell death caused by excessive Cu accumulation in cells, has emerged as a promising avenue for OS treatment. Excessive Cu induces abnormal oligomerization of lipoylated proteins and loss of iron-sulfur cluster proteins, which is correlated with the mitochondrial tricarboxylic acid cycle, thereby resulting in proteotoxic stress and triggering cell death, especially those are highly dependent on oxidative phosphorylation. This review aims to comprehensively summarize and discuss recent advancements in targeting cuproptosis in OS, highlighting its potential as a treatment strategy. We further discuss diverse approaches, including copper ionophores, nanomedicine, and combination therapies, which could induce cuproptosis in OS. We also delved into nanomaterial-mediated cuproptosis and nanodrug delivery systems. We further explore the strategies for enhancing therapeutic specificity and synergistic cancer therapeutics, such as ferroptosis, photothermal therapy, and immunotherapy. Moreover, the connection between cuproptosis and chemoresistance in OS is involved, demonstrating its potential to overcome treatment failure. In conclusion, targeting the copper metabolism pathways, either alone or in combination with existing therapies, may offer more effective treatment options for patients with OS.

items.title: Antigen-Presenting Microrobots Program CAR-T Cell Function.
items.abstract: Mechanical forces are emerging as key regulators of T-cell function, yet how active motion- derived mechanical cues from artificial antigen-presenting cells (aAPCs) influence T-cell activation and fate remains largely unexplored. Here, we develop self-propelled antigen-presenting microrobots (CytoBots)-gas-driven magnesium microparticles functionalized with anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 antibodies-that actively navigate suspension environments and mechanically engage T cells. Unlike immotile aAPCs, CytoBots generate motion-dependent, force-bearing stimulation that enhances T-cell activation. Single-cell force spectroscopy shows that CytoBots double receptor-ligand binding strength and extend bond lifetime threefold, supporting a role for motion-enhanced mechanical interactions in T-cell activation. CytoBot stimulation is associated with enhanced proximal T-cell signaling, increased phosphorylation of AKT and mTOR, and metabolic changes characterized by elevated mitochondrial respiration and glycolysis-associated activity. These responses accompany the enrichment of stem-like and central memory T-cell populations. In humanized tumor models, CytoBot-expanded CAR-T cells exhibit superior cytotoxicity, persistence, and antitumor efficacy. These findings establish microrobotic antigen-presenting interfaces as a generalizable strategy for programming immune cell function through dynamic mechanotransduction, opening new opportunities for next-generation cell therapies.

items.title: Clinical Spectrum and Early Warning of Severe Immune-Related Adverse Events Associated With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Narrative Review With Practice-Oriented Recommendations.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), including monoclonal antibodies targeting cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 (CTLA-4), programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1), and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), have fundamentally transformed the oncological treatment landscape. However, these agents disrupt immunological self-tolerance, giving rise to a distinctive spectrum of immune-related adverse events (irAEs) that can affect virtually every organ system. Severe irAEs (grade 3-4 per Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events) occur in approximately 10-30% of patients receiving ICI monotherapy and up to 55-60% of those receiving combination regimens, with fatality rates ranging from 0.3% to 1.3% depending on the agent class. This narrative review synthesises and critically appraises the available evidence on the clinical spectrum, pathogenesis, early warning biomarkers, and management of severe irAEs. Unlike previous reviews that have focused on individual organ systems or biomarker categories in isolation, this review integrates mechanistic insights, organ-specific clinical profiles, temporal patterns, candidate biomarkers, and risk-adapted management into a single practice-oriented framework, with particular emphasis on distinguishing established clinical guidance from investigational concepts. We examine the immunological mechanisms underpinning irAE development, including disruption of peripheral T-cell tolerance, cross-reactivity between tumour and host-tissue antigens, activation of autoreactive B cells, dysregulated cytokine signalling, and alterations in gut microbiota composition. Organ-specific manifestations-encompassing severe colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, myocarditis, endocrinopathies, neurotoxicity, nephritis, musculoskeletal toxicities, haematological toxicities, dermatological toxicities, and ocular toxicities-are discussed with reference to their epidemiology, temporal profiles, and prognostic implications. We evaluate both established and emerging circulating and tissue-based biomarkers for early risk stratification, including high-sensitivity cardiac troponins, faecal calprotectin, inflammatory cytokines, autoantibodies, peripheral blood eosinophil counts, and T-cell receptor repertoire diversity, critically appraising their clinical readiness and current limitations. Finally, we present practice-oriented recommendations for risk-adapted baseline assessment, serial monitoring, graded management algorithms, and multidisciplinary care coordination. This synthesis aims to provide clinicians with a practical framework for the anticipation, early detection, and management of severe irAEs, thereby supporting the therapeutic benefit of ICIs whilst safeguarding patient safety. Prospective validation of many of the biomarker strategies and monitoring protocols discussed herein remains an important priority for future research.
items.journal: Cancer control : journal of the Moffitt Cancer Center

items.title: RNA interference and antisense strategies for chronic hepatitis B: mechanisms, clinical advances, and pathways toward functional cure.
items.abstract: Current Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) therapies, nucleos(t)ide analogs and interferon (IFN), suppress viral replication but cannot eliminate covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) or integrated HBV DNA, leaving CHB a global health threat. High antigen levels cause profound immune exhaustion, so agents must silence viral transcripts while restoring antiviral immunity. This review summarizes RNA interference (RNAi) platforms as emerging therapies. Preclinical and phase I-II data show that GalNAc-conjugated siRNAs (xalnesiran, imdusiran, elebsiran, daplusiran/tomligisiran, RBD-1016) reduce HBsAg by 1-2 log IU/mL, often for months after treatment. By targeting transcripts from both cccDNA and integrated HBV DNA, they offer a mechanistic advantage over current antivirals. Combinations with capsid assembly modulators, pegylated IFN, therapeutic vaccines, or antisense drugs yield additive or synergistic declines in antigen, supporting RNAi as a backbone for curative multidrug regimens. Despite promising safety and efficacy, obstacles remain: HBsAg plateaus, incomplete immune restoration, delivery challenges in advanced liver disease, and lack of biomarkers for patient selection. Nevertheless, RNAi therapies represent a paradigm-shifting strategy that could move CHB care toward a finite, immune-driven functional cure. A literature search was conducted using Google Scholar for articles on RNAi and antisense strategies for CHB (1985-2026). Chronic hepatitis B is a long-term liver infection affecting around 296 million people worldwide, which can lead to serious liver damage and cancer. Current treatments control the virus but rarely cure it, because the virus leaves behind stubborn genetic material inside liver cells that keeps producing viral proteins. One of these proteins, called HBsAg, builds up in the blood and weakens the body’s immune defenses, making it harder for the immune system to fight the infection. A new group of medicines called RNA interference (RNAi) therapies works differently. Instead of simply blocking the virus from multiplying, these treatments act like molecular scissors, destroying the virus’s genetic instructions and sharply reducing viral protein production. This gives the immune system a chance to recover and fight back. Several of these medicines are now being tested in people, and results are encouraging. They can dramatically lower surface antigen levels, sometimes for many months after treatment stops. However, when used alone, they rarely eliminate the virus, and antigen levels tend to return after treatment ends. The most promising path forward appears to be combining RNAi with other treatments, such as antivirals, immune-stimulating drugs, or vaccines. These combinations have produced better results than any single drug. Researchers are also working on ways to predict which patients will respond best, so they can tailor treatment to each person. While challenges remain, RNAi is reshaping how we think about curing hepatitis B, moving toward a future where the infection can be controlled or even cured.

items.title: First Molecular Detection of Hepatitis E Virus (HEV) RNA in Red Deer from Piedmont and Lombardy Regions (Italy): Potential Implications for Zoonotic Transmission.
items.abstract: Paslahepevirus balayani (hepatitis E virus, HEV) is the causative agent of hepatitis E, a zoonotic disease of global public health concern. In Europe, human infections are mainly associated with genotype 3 (HEV-3), frequently linked to the consumption of raw or undercooked meat and meat products. Although pigs and wild boars are recognized as the main HEV reservoirs, the epidemiological role of deer remains unclear. This study investigated HEV RNA occurrence and genetic characteristics in red deer ( Cervus elaphus ) hunted in Piedmont and Lombardy, Italy. A total of 170 liver samples and 40 paired muscle samples from a subset of the same animals were analysed using touchdown RT-PCR followed by touchdown hemi-nested PCR. HEV RNA was detected in 22/170 liver samples (12.94%; 95% CI: 8.70-18.82%) and 3/40 muscle samples (7.50%; 95% CI: 2.58-19.86%). Partial HEV sequences were successfully obtained from 19 liver samples, and all were assigned to genotype 3 subtype 3c (HEV-3c). The three PCR-positive muscle samples were not sequence-confirmed. To our knowledge, this is the first molecular detection of HEV RNA in red deer from the sampled areas of Piedmont and Lombardy. These findings provide new data on HEV circulation in red deer in Northern Italy and highlight potential implications for food safety and public health.

items.title: Epidemiology and Ecological Prevention and Control of Diseases in Traditionally Raised Tibetan Pigs: A Review.
items.abstract: The Tibetan pig ( Sus scrofa domesticus ) is raised under extensive, free-range conditions on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, where it is exposed to a distinctive epidemiological landscape. In this narrative review, we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, CNKI and Wanfang for surveys published between 1990 and 2026, extracted study-level estimates together with their denominators, assays and settings, and summarized the major diseases of Tibetan pigs and the ecological options for their control. Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus is the best-documented viral pathogen, with 38.3% RNA detection in feces ( n = 193) and 39.6% seroprevalence in Nyingchi, followed by swine influenza A virus (52.0% H1N1 seropositivity; n = 421) and diarrheagenic Escherichia coli ; because these figures come from different assays and populations, they are reported side-by-side rather than compared or pooled. Gastrointestinal parasites are widespread, with 90.1% prevalence in grazing herds and 60.1% in corralled herds ( n = 715; an unadjusted comparison from a single Nyingchi survey). African swine fever reached Nyingchi in 2019, showing the vulnerability of extensive systems to transboundary epidemics. Zoonotic and potentially zoonotic agents, including hepatitis E virus, Toxoplasma gondii , Trichinella spp., Echinococcus granulosus and Enterocytozoon bieneusi , circulate at the livestock-wildlife-human interface. Age, housing and grazing mode, and the frequency of deworming and vaccination have been associated with infection outcomes in individual surveys, although their independent contributions remain poorly quantified. We propose, as an evidence-informed framework that remains to be validated, an integrated ecological approach spanning landscape and ecosystem, herd and farm, animal and host, surveillance and information, and governance under One Health, which adapts biosecurity to plateau production while seeking to preserve the genetic resilience and gut microbiome of the breed. Key gaps include the absence of systematic serosurveys, limited cohort data, and unquantified antimicrobial resistance dynamics in free-ranging herds.

items.title: The RdRp Thumb-1 Pocket Is a Conserved Target for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Development.
items.abstract: RNA viruses cause human diseases ranging from mild colds to deadly pandemics. Direct-acting, broad-spectrum, non-nucleoside antivirals have been characterized as impossible to develop because allosteric binding sites are poorly conserved. The HCV NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) Thumb-1 allosteric site and its interaction with the HCV NS5B Λ1-loop governs an essential conformational change required for polymerase initiation. The only approved NS5B Thumb-1 inhibitor, beclabuvir, has been shown to be inactive against a broad panel of non-HCV viruses, including poliovirus, rhinovirus, coronavirus, coxsackievirus, influenzavirus, and HIV. A conserved, homologous allosteric site on RdRp that spans multiple viral families has not been reported. Here, we report GALILEO's discovery that the Thumb-1 pocket, its associated Λ1-loop and their interaction are conserved between RNA viral families for the first time. The discovery is structurally validated through comparative analysis of Protein Data Bank (PDB)-deposited viral polymerases utilizing a method that allows independent, public validation. We further demonstrate that beclabuvir's dependence on its indole C6 carbonyl to interact with the HCV-specific residue R 503 restricts its activity to HCV. The discovery is biochemically validated with MDL-001, which does not contain a C6 carbonyl substituent. MDL-001 directly blocks viral RNA synthesis in isolated HCV and SARS-CoV-2 replication complexes and selects for the canonical Thumb-1 resistance mutation P495S in HCV NS5B. The discovery is validated at the cellular level through demonstration of MDL-001's broad-spectrum, in vitro inhibition of both HCV and SARS-CoV-2. Preclinical proof of concept and development of MDL-001 in HCV, HBV, HDV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV have been previously reported. These findings establish RdRp Thumb-1 as a conserved allosteric pocket and a druggable target for broad-spectrum direct-acting antiviral development.

items.title: Mammary and brain pharmacokinetics of licochalcone A after oral and intravenous administration: implications for breast cancer prevention and interception.
items.abstract: Licochalcone A (LicA), a prenylated chalcone from Glycyrrhiza inflata , shows promising anti-tumor activity in breast cancer models, but translation is limited by poor bioavailability and rapid systemic clearance. Oral delivery is the clinically favored route for long-term use of breast cancer prevention drugs in women at elevated risk of developing breast cancer. We report the first validated quantification of LicA in mammary tissue in a prevention context and the first characterization of brain distribution under intact blood-brain barrier (BBB) conditions for intercepting brain metastasis. Formulations spanning aqueous (F07), lipid-based (L05), surfactant-rich (L13) and co-solvent (L022, L024) systems were selected by solubility screening and simulated gastrointestinal re-dispersibility. Eight independent pharmacokinetic studies were conducted across two species. Plasma, mammary, brain, and liver were quantified. Subcutaneous L022 (80 mg/kg/day, 28 days) that suppressed tumor growth in mice, presented a trough plasma LicA of 68 ng/mL (IQR 35-105), below in vitro -effective thresholds. Oral L024 in mice was rapidly absorbed (T max 0.25-0.5 h, plasma C max 817 ng/mL) and achieved mammary (C max 1,093 ng/g), with tissue-to-plasma partitioning (Kp) > 1 by every metric at 100 mg/kg. Brain-to-plasma Kp remained 0.3-0.5 after oral dosing but exceeded 1 from 1 h after intravenous dosing, reaching 3.92 at 8 h, while brain C max rose from 378 to 9,925 ng/g. Dose-normalized plasma exposure was 37-fold lower after oral than intravenous administration and brain exposure fell almost proportionally, by 27.5-fold. We interpret this as indicating that limited oral brain exposure reflects pre-systemic loss rather than restricted BBB transfer, although transfer kinetics were not measured directly. In rats, F07 was constrained by low drug-loading, while L05 and L13 achieved higher loading and prolonged T 1/2 but were only characterized in plasma. L13 was not tolerated intravenously in pre-study tolerability assessment, and L05 was not advanced on formulation-development grounds rather than on pharmacokinetic performance. L024 was tolerated by both routes and was the only formulation for which tissue distribution data. It was selected as the lead candidate for chronic evaluation on the basis of tissue distribution data and dual-route tolerability. L024s short half-life predicts a low once-daily steady-state trough, addressable by divided dosing.

items.title: Integrated RRBS profiling links copy-number concordance to methylation divergence in recurrent liver tumors.
items.abstract: To examine whether broad copy-number alteration (CNA) signals inferred from high-depth reduced-representation bisulfite sequencing (RRBS) can be integrated with DNA methylation profiles to characterize structural and epigenetic divergence in matched original and recurrent liver tumors. Unique molecular identifier (UMI)-corrected RRBS data from 10 patients were reanalyzed. Non-redundant fragment counts and methylation values were summarized in 100-kb bins. Original tumor-recurrent tumor (OT-RT) CNA relatedness was quantified by rC, integrating Pearson correlation of log 2 copy-number ratios with CNA state concordance. Genome-wide methylation divergence, regional CNA-methylation coupling (CMC), and adult-liver chromatin annotations were evaluated. rC captured variation in tumor-pair CNA relatedness, with descriptive groupings designated clonal-like, clonally diverged, or independent-like. Lower rC was associated with greater OT-RT methylation divergence ( r  =  -0.903, p  = 3.40 × 10 -4 ). Pooled CMC was modestly negative ( r  =  -0.104; permutation p  < 0.001), but local correlations occurred in both directions. Positive CMC was less frequent and localized to liver-active regulatory chromatin, whereas negative CMC was more prevalent in relatively repressive contexts. This proof-of-concept analysis supports the use of high-depth RRBS for integrated analysis of broad structural and epigenetic variation in recurrent liver tumors, revealing coordinated patient-level divergence and chromatin-context-dependent regional coupling. Liver tumors can return after treatment, but a recurrent tumor may be closely related to the original tumor or may have developed more independently. Cancer cells can show large gains or losses of DNA as well as changes in DNA methylation, a chemical modification that helps regulate gene activity. We reanalyzed sequencing data from 10 patients with matched original and recurrent liver tumors. The same sequencing data were used to estimate broad DNA copy-number patterns and DNA methylation. Tumor pairs with more similar copy-number profiles generally showed smaller genome-wide differences in DNA methylation between the original and recurrent tumors. When copy number and methylation were compared across the genome, their overall relationship was modest but varied by genomic region. Regions with positive and negative relationships tended to occur in different types of liver chromatin. These findings suggest that structural DNA changes and methylation changes are related during recurrent liver tumor development, but they are not identical measures of tumor evolution. Because only 10 patient pairs were studied and the copy-number estimates were not validated with a separate genomic test, larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Strictly-adherent gut microbiota form a distinct ecological niche in the colorectal compartment of human gastrointestinal tract.
items.abstract: The gut microbiome exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity along the gastrointestinal tract (GIT), yet most human studies rely on fecal samples, which may not accurately represent mucosa-adherent microbial communities. In particular, the strictly adherent microbiota, residing in close proximity to the intestinal epithelium and immune cells, remain poorly characterized. We compared fecal, loosely adherent, and strictly adherent microbiota in 60 colorectal cancer patients undergoing surgery with curative intent. Preoperative fecal samples, intraoperative mucosal swabs, and resected macroscopically tumor-free intestinal tissue from colonic and rectal sites were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. After accounting for strong interindividual variability, fecal microbiota closely resembled the loosely adherent mucosal microbiota, supporting feces as a reliable proxy for this compartment throughout the GIT. In contrast, strictly adherent communities were compositionally distinct and characterized by a conserved enrichment of oxygen-tolerant taxa, including Bacillus and Lactobacillus , across anatomical sites. Additional regional variation was observed within the strictly adherent niche, with select taxa displaying higher relative abundances in the rectum compared with the right colon. Together, these findings demonstrate that strictly adherent microbiota represent a distinct and structured ecological niche that is only partially captured by conventional fecal or mucosal sampling, underscoring the importance of sampling strategy and anatomical location in gut microbiome research.

items.title: Beyond resection: liver transplantation in biliary malignancies.
items.abstract: Biliary malignancies comprise a heterogeneous group of tumors with distinct anatomic locations and biologic behaviors. Although surgical resection remains the standard curative-intent treatment, liver transplantation (LT) has emerged in selected settings, making it important to define when transplantation is justified. PubMed searches for English-language literature, without a lower publication-date restriction, were updated through 22 September 2026, supplemented by reference lists, current society guidelines, consensus statements, and organ-allocation policy documents. This review examines LT for perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (pCCA), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma (cHCC-CCA), gallbladder cancer, and distal extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. We discuss historical evolution, selection criteria, neoadjuvant strategies, outcomes and pretransplant dropout, technical morbidity after neoadjuvant radiotherapy, allocation policy, living-donor considerations, and future directions. The strongest evidence supports LT for highly selected, protocol-compliant pCCA; for iCCA, LT remains an emerging, biology-driven indication limited to two distinct settings: very early incidental tumors in cirrhosis or unresectable liver-confined disease with durable stability after systemic therapy. cHCC-CCA remains selected and controversial, and evidence is insufficient to support routine LT for gallbladder cancer or distal extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma; expansion should be guided by biologic selection rather than by anatomic considerations alone.
